model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Both the model name and the evaluator model record this evaluating session's actual runtime identity, Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. The agent definition's pinned evaluator value was deliberately not copied here (#1058): the pin selects an evaluator, this block states which one actually ran, and a score is only comparable to another score produced by the same evaluator.

issues_detected.description: Two different project end dates are asserted in the same record and never reconciled. collection_timeframes cites NIH RePORTER for a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, while collection_timeframes, updates and missing_data_documentation all state that data collection and quarterly release continue 'through the end of the project in November 2026'. A user planning around the release cadence cannot tell which end date governs.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a source_caveats entry reconciling the RePORTER award period with the stated November 2026 project end, or attribute each date to its source and say which is preferred, as the record already does for the June 2026 release date.

issues_detected.description: Version scopes are mixed. Top-level version is '2.0' for this June 2026 release, while version_access lists the earlier October 2025 and June 2025 releases as 'Version 2.1'. Read literally, two superseded releases carry a higher version number than the current one. version_details explains that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with its own internal version history, which resolves the mechanism, but the top-level version slot still reads as a release-series version.
issues_detected.recommendation: State in version_access that the numbers are per-dataset Dataverse revisions and are not comparable across releases, or qualify the top-level version as the Dataverse revision of this dataset specifically.

issues_detected.description: Most preprocessing, cleaning and labeling detail describes the MuSIC pipeline, and each entry carries a source_caveat stating that the pipeline's computed cell maps are not included in this release. The processing actually applied to the distributed archives is therefore covered only by one cleaning entry (quality control before release) and the FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate validation. The disclosure is candid and correctly scoped, but a reuser cannot reconstruct how the released archives themselves were produced from raw instrument output.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add preprocessing entries for the released artifacts themselves: peptide/protein identification and quantification settings for the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, image acquisition and export settings for the immunofluorescence archives, and the alignment and count-matrix pipeline for the perturb-seq archives.

issues_detected.description: The distribution format is stated only as the container. format gives 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with media_type application/zip, and no field names the file formats inside the archives (image format, mass spectrometry format, single-cell matrix format). The packaging layer is well specified through RO-Crate, JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema; the payload layer is not.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the internal file formats per archive, and populate encoding where text formats are involved, so a reuser can plan ingestion before downloading multi-gigabyte archives.

issues_detected.description: Grant identifiers are recorded as fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#grant-1OT2OD032742-01) with the actual award number held in prose notes. The award numbers themselves are correct and follow NIH activity-code format, but no slot carries the award number as a machine-readable value.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the NIH award number in a dedicated award identifier slot in addition to the minted fragment id, so funding can be matched programmatically to RePORTER.

issues_detected.description: The Dataverse programmatic access URL is a base path with no file identifier (https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/), so it is not directly resolvable. It documents the API route rather than providing a retrievable link. The landing page URL is complete and correct.
issues_detected.recommendation: Show the pattern with a placeholder for the file id, or link the Dataverse data access API documentation page.

issues_detected.description: The publisher slot is empty by a documented evidential decision recorded in source_caveats, on the grounds that the bundle names no publisher. The hosting platform is nonetheless stated unambiguously in the citation ('University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'), in page, in maintainers and in data_governance, so the information is present in the record while the dedicated slot is not.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) as publisher with a caveat that the attribution is taken from the citation the landing page prints, rather than leaving the slot empty.

issues_detected.description: Nine of the 47 creators are identified by fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI, with names and affiliations held only in prose notes, and five University of Virginia authors carry a ROR affiliation with no institution name. The record documents both decisions explicitly, so this is a transparent limitation of the source rather than a fabrication, but those creator entries are not machine-resolvable to a person.
issues_detected.recommendation: Where an ORCID cannot be established from the bundle, carry the person's name in a name slot rather than only in notes, so the entry is readable without parsing prose.

semantic_insights: The DOI, the id, the citation and the persistentId embedded in the landing page URL all resolve to the same value, 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, with no drift between them.

The DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) prefix, which matches the repository named in the citation and the landing page host, so the identifier is plausible as well as well formed.

Two cell line RRIDs are given in Cellosaurus form, RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J. CVCL_ is the correct namespace for cell lines; the SCR_ and AB_ prefixes named in the rubric would be wrong here.
total_file_count of 10 reconciles exactly with the file_collections counts, 3 immunofluorescence plus 2 AP-MS plus 2 SEC-MS plus 2 perturb-seq plus 1 metadata archive.

The license position is internally coherent across four slots: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license, data_use_permission no_commercial_use, a commercial-use prohibition in prohibited_uses, and the ShareAlike condition restated in ip_restrictions.
ethical_reviews.contact_person is ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, which matches the Ravitsky V entry in the creators list. The cross-reference resolves within the record.

The record distinguishes release scope from project scope where the sources conflate them, holding the portal's cumulative totals (21.4 TB, 53,788 images, 7,023 proteins) in notes rather than asserting them of this release.

Where the June 2026 file listing carries no per-file descriptions, the record declines to carry forward the 464-protein count from the October 2025 release and gives the reason: the archives report identical file sizes but different MD5 checksums, so they were regenerated. That is an evidence-grounded refusal rather than a gap.
Temporal ordering is valid: created_on 2025-02-27 precedes issued 2026-06-17, and the 2026-07-15 second publication date for the image archives is recorded in distribution_dates with its explanation.

The dataset is correctly characterized as non-human-subjects throughout. direct_collection.is_direct is false with the explicit statement that data were not collected from individuals, human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false, and sensitive_elements_present is false with a reasoned justification. These three agree with each other and with the cell-line description.

known_biases uses the BiasTypeEnum categories representation_bias and selection_bias, and the representation_bias description is the same statement carried in sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, so the bias claim and the sampling claim do not diverge.

correctness_validations.notes: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C matches 10.XXXX/... and the prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse, consistent with the named host. Grant numbers 1OT2OD032742-01, OT2OD032742, 3OT2OD032742-01S2 and 5U54HG012513-02 all follow NIH activity-code format. RRIDs are Cellosaurus cell-line identifiers, correctly formed for their namespace. All URLs are well structured on plausible domains; the Dataverse API access URL is a base path with no file identifier and so is not directly resolvable.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI matches the 10.XXXX/... pattern and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse, the repository the citation and landing page name. Two Cellosaurus RRIDs are additionally carried for the source cell lines. Identifier, id slot and landing page URL agree.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of roughly 1,700 characters naming both cell lines, the three treatment conditions, four differentiation states and all four assay modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: Well past the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: it names MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J, the paclitaxel and vorinostat arms, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS and immunofluorescence, the RO-Crate and FAIRSCAPE packaging, and the stated scientific objective.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 29 terms including CM4AI, Bridge2AI, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, subcellular imaging, paclitaxel, vorinostat
sub_elements.quality_note: Far above the 5-keyword threshold, and the terms span program, assay, cell line, perturbation and analysis method rather than repeating the title.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections gives five named collections with ids, file counts, sizes and compression
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page resolves against the named repository, and file_collections supplies a genuine hierarchical resource structure whose counts sum to the declared total_file_count of 10.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of entries (October 2025, June 2025, March 2025 and the original release), two is_described_by preprints, one references entry
sub_elements.quality_note: The full quarterly release lineage is expressed with typed relationships and target DOIs, and the entry whose portal association is uncertain carries a source_caveat saying so.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spelling out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 obligations; ip_restrictions listing four restrictions including Regents of the University of California copyright and Stanford copyright on the raw image data
sub_elements.quality_note: The access policy is stated with its permissions and its four license conditions, and the IP position is allocated by data package, naming which institution holds copyright over what and where commercial licensing is negotiated.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: unrestricted; two regulatory_restrictions entries; other_compliance naming FAIR compliance as an NIH requirement and Jillian Parker as the Data Governance Committee contact
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitivity is classified explicitly and the two restrictions are substantive: the non-human-subjects, de-identified, not-FDA-regulated determination, and an affirmative constraint that clinical or patient-care use requires regulatory oversight and approval. HIPAA fields are correctly absent for a non-human-subjects cell-line dataset.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: the Dataverse landing page and https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, described as recommended for archives above the web download size limit
sub_elements.quality_note: No dedicated download_url slot is populated, but the landing page gives working access and the API route is documented with the reason to use it for the multi-gigabyte image archives. The API URL is a base path without a file identifier, which is noted as an issue rather than treated as a failure.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata', media_type application/zip; each file_collection records compression: zip
sub_elements.quality_note: A valid MIME type is given and the packaging is named precisely. The formats of the files inside the archives are never stated, which is recorded as a separate semantic issue.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources across five groups: two preprints with DOIs, MassIVE and Figshare deposits, the embargoed perturb-seq links, the CM4AI portal, and the Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE and IMP software links; related_datasets with seven typed entries
sub_elements.quality_note: External links are grouped by kind, marked archival or not, and the embargoed group carries both a restriction statement and a source_caveat explaining why the June 2026 embargo statement is preferred over the June 2025 SRA links.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met on external fields: distribution_formats is populated with two entries, page and access_urls link an accessible Dataverse record, and the license explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit...'; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use
sub_elements.quality_note: A named standard license with its URL, its four conditions stated, and the commercial carve-out routed to a specific negotiation path. A reuser can determine what is permitted without leaving the record.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated and the Dataverse landing page is openly accessible with no access request required per data_governance.
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata; media_type: application/zip; conforms_to names JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema serializations with dataset schemas resolvable from package metadata
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the packaging layer, which is standardized and machine-resolvable through RO-Crate with JSON-Schema dataset schemas. The internal payload formats are not named, which is why this is a pass with a recorded semantic issue rather than a clean one. No encoding slot is populated.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible landing page, reuse-permitting license.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate with ARK persistent identifiers and end-to-end provenance in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology; conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology terms
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the packaging standard, the provenance ontology, and the datasheet schema itself, with ontology term identifiers used for substrate and topic rather than free text.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible landing page, reuse-permitting license.
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot is populated anywhere in the record. The closest content is file_collections, which describes archives at the collection level, and instances, which describes measurement types.
sub_elements.quality_note: Absent, and the information is absent from the record rather than merely misplaced. A reuser cannot learn what columns or fields the released tables carry without downloading and opening an archive.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four categories with usage_notes; discouraged_uses: three entries; prohibited_uses: three prohibition_reason entries covering clinical decision-making, commercial use and non-ShareAlike redistribution
sub_elements.quality_note: All three guidance kinds are populated and each entry gives a reason rather than a bare label. The discouragement against analyses requiring integrated cell maps is tied to the specific fact that computed maps are excluded from this release.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Applicability was resolved per sub-element, not once for the element (#1060). Sub-elements 1 and 2 carry the governance disjunct and are applicable here; sub-elements 3 to 5 ask about participants, of which this dataset has none, and are excluded. The two questions were resolved against different conditions and reached different answers, which is the point of the per-sub-element gate.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects condition NOT met: description and keywords name cell lines, assays and disease contexts but no participants, patients or clinical research; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes endogenous tagging, chromatography, robot-assisted staining and CRISPR screens, never recruitment. Governance condition MET on E2 fields: regulatory_restrictions carries an affirmative constraint, 'Use of these laboratory data in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care requires appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and other_compliance states ethical conditions of release and names a Data Governance Committee contact. This is a constraint that applies, not a record that none applies, so the disjunct is satisfied and the sub-element is scored. E4's own fields were not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews with reviewing_organization 'CM4AI Ethics module' and contact_person ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, describing Value-Sensitive Design methodology, an axiological repository of values and a CM4AI Life Cycle governance framework; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board naming Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon; data_governance.access_review_process and five stewardship_roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical oversight is documented substantively for a dataset with no participants: a named review body, two named review contacts, a governance committee contact, a described access and dual-licensing review process, and a stated methodology. The absence of IRB approval is explained rather than left blank, and the explanation is consistent with involves_human_subjects being false. The record also refuses to equate the 'Data Governance Committee' the release names with the 'Data Access Committee' the preprint anticipates, recording the distinction in source_caveats instead.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same resolution as sub-element 1. Human subjects condition NOT met on E1 description/keywords or E8 collection_mechanisms; governance condition MET on E2 regulatory_restrictions, which states an affirmative clinical-use constraint and names ethical conditions of release with a governance contact. Deidentification is a meaningful question for donor-derived cell lines even with no participants, which is why this sub-element carries the governance disjunct. E4's own is_deidentified block was not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with deidentification_details: 'The release states that samples are de-identified... such data are non-clinical and are considered de-identified because they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; raw_data_sources names the provenance of both lines, ATCC and the HipSci resource
sub_elements.quality_note: The basis of the de-identification determination is stated and is semantically appropriate for the data type: the material is donor-derived cell lines obtained through established repositories, so the claim rests on non-linkability rather than on an applied technique. No named technique such as Safe Harbor or k-anonymity appears, correctly, because none was applied. The 'with current knowledge' qualifier is an honest limit on the claim rather than an overstatement.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition not met and no governance disjunct available for this sub-element. Description and keywords name cell lines, assays, drugs and disease contexts with no participant, patient or clinical-research terms; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes laboratory assays on cell lines, not recruitment. The Data Governance Committee contact and the access review process are a governance structure, which #1060 states is not a participant signal for this sub-element. Independently corroborated by direct_collection.is_direct: false, 'Data were not collected from individuals'.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants exist in this dataset, so there is no participant privacy to protect and no participant re-identification risk to assess.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter, laboratory measurements on commercial cell lines, rather than the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition not met, same evidence as sub-element 3: no participant, patient or clinical-research terms in description or keywords; collection_mechanisms describes AP-MS on tagged lines, SEC-MS, robot-assisted immunofluorescence staining and CRISPRi screens, none of which is recruitment. A governance structure does not make this sub-element applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants were enrolled, so there is no consent procedure, consent type or withdrawal mechanism to document.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Consent from the original cell line donors is a matter for the source repositories, ATCC and HipSci, not for this release, and the record correctly points to those provenance routes instead of asserting a consent process of its own.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition not met, same evidence as sub-elements 3 and 4. No at-risk population was enrolled and no one was compensated, because no one participated. A governance structure is not a participant signal.
sub_elements.evidence: No at_risk_populations or participant_compensation content is possible for a dataset with no human participants.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Note that donor characteristics are nonetheless disclosed where they bear on representativeness, in known_biases.affected_subsets and raw_data_sources, which is the right place for them.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources describing MDA-MB-468 as established from a pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma and KOLF2.1J as derived from a healthy male Northern European donor; known_biases.affected_subsets naming both lines; sampling_strategies describing the selection of two disease-relevant lines and the panel of perturbations
sub_elements.quality_note: No subpopulations slot is populated, but the analogue for a cell-line dataset is fully described: donor characteristics for both lines, the treatment and differentiation arms that define the subsets, and the inclusion rationale for each. The information is present and specific, not merely relocated boilerplate.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10; file_collections with file_count 3, 2, 2, 2 and 1 and per-archive sizes of 4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB, 113.3 KB, 135.8 KB, 171.8 KB, 93.9 KB, 30.2 KB, 73.3 KB and 1.1 MB; instances recording 11,739 targeted genes in the KOLF2.1J atlas; collection_mechanisms recording 17 tagged genes with 34 more in progress and 6 guide RNAs per gene
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are specific and reconcile arithmetically. Where a count cannot be established for this release, notably the number of proteins imaged, the record says so and explains why the October 2025 figure was not carried forward.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot and no is_tabular slot are populated. file_collections describes archives; instances describes measurement types; neither reaches variable or column level.
sub_elements.quality_note: Absent from the record entirely. This is the same gap as Element 3 sub-element 4 and is the record's clearest structural weakness: the composition can be understood at the archive and modality level but not at the field level.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances: four entries with data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:15, :28, :26 and :12 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:56, :59, :58 and :64, each with a detailed instance_type description including the four-channel staining scheme for the imaging data
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are carried as ontology term identifiers rather than free text, and the accompanying prose specifies the disease contexts, the cell types and the perturbation conditions each instance type covers.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies with is_sample true, is_random false, is_representative false and a why_not_representative statement; missing_data_documentation giving missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy; source_caveats noting that the image archives report identical file sizes but different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 release
sub_elements.quality_note: Sampling is characterized honestly, including the explicit non-representativeness flags, and the missing-data account is specific: no computed cell maps, incompletely overlapping protein panels across modalities, embargoed perturb-seq links, and AP-MS present only for treated MDA-MB-468 cells. The MD5 observation is a genuine anomaly detected and reported rather than smoothed over.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met on external fields: distribution_formats populated, page resolves to an open Dataverse record, data_governance states no access request is required, license permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'
sub_elements.quality_note: A version number is present and agrees with the V2 in the citation. Its scope relative to the prior releases' internal version numbers is recorded as a consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; versions_available listing all five releases with their DOIs; version_details explaining that quarterly releases are separate Dataverse datasets each with its own DOI and internal version history
sub_elements.quality_note: Every prior version is reachable by DOI, and the mechanism by which versions are published and retained is explained, including that files are not removed from previously published versions.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: No errata slot is populated. updates.update_details describes what future releases will add rather than what this release changed. The only backward-looking change note is the source_caveats observation that the image archives were regenerated.
sub_elements.quality_note: No change log relates this release to the October 2025 release it supersedes. A user upgrading from the prior release cannot tell what changed, which matters here because the image archives were regenerated with identical sizes and different checksums, a change the record notices but does not describe as an erratum.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: Quarterly; update_details: 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis', naming computed cell maps, iPSC immunofluorescence images and further AP-MS interactomes as forthcoming
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a cadence and an end horizon are given, and the planned additions are named specifically. The horizon conflicts with the RePORTER project period elsewhere in the record, which is recorded as a consistency failure.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources with four entries covering both cell lines with RRIDs and access routes and both repository deposits; conforms_to describing ARK identifiers and end-to-end provenance in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology; related_datasets giving the four-release lineage; data_collectors attributing each modality to a named laboratory
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is documented in both directions: upstream to the cell lines and the raw mass spectrometry and sequence deposits, and structurally through the RO-Crate provenance graph. Each assay modality is attributed to the specific laboratory that produced it.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses covering spatiotemporal cell architecture mapping, machine-readable hierarchical maps as AI-ready data, visible machine learning, and ethical AI-ready packaging; addressing_gaps: three responses on black-box models, uncharted subcellular architecture and the absence of an operational AI-readiness definition
sub_elements.quality_note: Motivation is stated as a scientific argument, not a mission statement, and addressing_gaps names the specific deficiencies the dataset is meant to close.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: hierarchical multi-scale cell map construction, training and evaluation of visible neural networks, variant interpretation against cellular components; other_tasks: protein complex mapping, differential elution profiling, CRISPRi phenotype analysis and integrative structure modeling with the Integrative Modeling Platform
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the headline objectives and the secondary analyses the individual data streams support are enumerated, with the modeling task described down to the ranking criteria used to select communities.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health; National Institutes of Health, Bridge2AI Bridge Center; Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia
sub_elements.quality_note: Three distinct funders with their mechanisms distinguished, and the entry with no grant identifier says so explicitly rather than leaving the omission unexplained.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: Award 1OT2OD032742-01; RePORTER core project OT2OD032742 with application 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, PI Trey Ideker, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, FY2025 award 5,289,382; Bridge Center award 5U54HG012513-02
sub_elements.quality_note: All award numbers follow NIH activity-code format, OT2 and U54 with the OD and HG institute codes, and are internally consistent across the parent and supplement numbers. The award numbers sit in prose notes under minted fragment identifiers rather than in a machine-readable award slot, which is recorded as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: 47 entries, 38 with ORCID identifiers and several with ROR affiliations; maintainers: three entries covering the point of contact, the program manager and the archival institution
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is thorough and its limits are declared: the record states that nine authors carry no ORCID in the bundle and are given fragment identifiers, and that five University of Virginia authors are recorded by ROR because the listing prints a ROR URL rather than an institution name.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified AND datasets shared. Collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods with four entries, collection_mechanisms with four entries), and the shared condition is met on distribution_formats, an accessible landing page and a reuse-permitting license.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries covering endogenous tagging of 17 genes with AP-MS under three conditions, SEC-MS across both lines and four differentiation states, robot-automated fixation and permeabilization with Human Protein Atlas antibodies and four-channel confocal microscopy, and CRISPRi lentiviral screens with 6 guide RNAs per gene read out on the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; collection_timeframes and data_collectors also populated
sub_elements.quality_note: Settings are given at a level that supports replication: antibody source, channel assignments, guide RNA density, readout kit and inducible dCas9 engineering. Each modality is attributed to the laboratory that performed it.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as sub-element 1: collection fields populated and the datasets shared condition met on external distribution and access fields.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries, each with was_directly_observed true and was_reported_by_subjects false, covering AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, SEC-MS as an orthogonal approach, ICC-IF with confocal microscopy, and single-cell CRISPRi screens; raw_data_sources naming ATCC, HipSci, MassIVE and the embargoed sequence deposits
sub_elements.quality_note: Instruments and techniques are named per modality and the observation flags are set consistently with a non-human-subjects dataset. Raw sources are traced to the repositories that hold them, with access status stated for each.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software condition met on E10 fields: external_resources references code repositories, specifically https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, plus the FAIRSCAPE framework at https://fairscape.github.io and the Integrative Modeling Platform. E8's own preprocessing fields were not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: four entries covering node2vec PPI embedding, Human Protein Atlas image embedding, contrastive co-embedding and community detection; cleaning_strategies: FAIRSCAPE input validation with JSON-Schema and quality control before release; labeling_strategies: alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome plus large language model naming with a confidence score
sub_elements.quality_note: The pipeline is described step by step with the specific models and reference resources named. Scored as a pass because the content is detailed and non-boilerplate, but with a recorded semantic issue: each entry carries a caveat that these steps produce the computed cell maps, which this release excludes, so processing of the released archives themselves is covered only by the release quality control and the RO-Crate validation.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as sub-element 3, met on E10 external_resources code repository references.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io, Integrative Modeling Platform at http://integrativemodeling.org; node2vec, the Human Protein Atlas deep learning model and the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit named in the processing and collection fields
sub_elements.quality_note: Named tools with resolvable repository and documentation links give a reuser an actionable route to the processing code. No software_and_tools slot is populated and no version is pinned for any tool, even though version_details asserts that the version used to produce each dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata. Scored as a pass on the strength of the repository links, with the missing version pins noted as a weakness.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met on external distribution and access fields, same evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: Two preprints with DOIs, doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 with PMCID PMC11580897; conforms_to naming RO-Crate, ARK, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema; the CM4AI portal and data releases page
sub_elements.quality_note: Publications carry resolvable identifiers, and standards are named at the packaging, provenance and schema layers rather than gestured at generically.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries covering scope_limitation (no computed cell maps in this interim release), coverage_limitation (incompletely overlapping protein panels), temporal_limitation (pre-publication embargo), methodological_limitation (domain expertise required) and coverage_limitation (imaging only for MDA-MB-468)
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, specific to this release rather than generic, and two carry a recommended_mitigation or scope_impact telling a user what to do about them, including the option of constructing maps from the released streams with the Cell Mapping Toolkit.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: representation_bias with affected_subsets naming both donor-derived lines, and selection_bias with a mitigation_strategy citing the expansion to a genome-scale screen of 11,739 genes; future_use_impacts: three entries on generalization limits, the Ethics module's governance framework and foreseeable clinical misuse
sub_elements.quality_note: Both entries use BiasTypeEnum categories, name the affected subsets, and one carries a concrete mitigation. future_use_impacts supplies the downstream social impact dimension, including the identification of unapproved clinical use as a foreseeable misuse.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot is populated. Data quality content appears elsewhere: missing_data_documentation covers gaps and embargoes, and source_caveats records that the image archives report identical file sizes but different MD5 checksums from the prior release.
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated anomalies slot is empty and no measurement-level quality issues are documented, such as batch effects across the three imaging conditions, mass spectrometry run variability or perturb-seq guide representation. The checksum observation is the closest thing to an anomaly report and it sits in prose caveats rather than in a slot a consumer would query.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with sensitivity_details explaining that the released content is laboratory measurements on commercially available cell lines rather than personal identifiers or protected health information
sub_elements.quality_note: An explicit, reasoned negative determination rather than an empty field, and it agrees with is_deidentified and human_subject_research. The reasoning names what the content actually is, so a reader can check the conclusion instead of taking it on trust.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: review_details describing the Ethics module's Value-Sensitive Design methodology, axiological value repository, CM4AI Life Cycle governance framework and mixed-methods empirical research, with reviewing_organization and an ORCID contact_person; data_governance.notes describing the ethical preparation and licensing plan and the Bridge2AI Code of Conduct
sub_elements.quality_note: Review documentation is substantive and attributed. Conflicts of interest are not addressed anywhere in the record, which is a gap, but the ethical review content itself is detailed enough to carry the sub-element.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met on external fields: distribution_formats populated, page resolves to an open Dataverse record, data_governance states no access request is required for the published files.
sub_elements.evidence: citation ends 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; page is a dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page; maintainers records the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) School of Medicine collection as archival steward; third_party_sharing additionally names MassIVE and Figshare
sub_elements.quality_note: The hosting platform is a recognized institutional repository and is identified unambiguously in four places. The dedicated publisher slot is empty by a documented decision recorded in source_caveats, on the grounds that the bundle names no publisher for the release; that is recorded as a low-severity structural issue, not a failure, because the information itself is present and actionable.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified AND datasets shared. external_resources references two publications with DOIs, doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, and related_datasets adds doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3; the shared condition is met on distribution and access fields.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full 47-author recommended citation with year, title, DOI URL, repository and version; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms.notes directs users to the data citation shown on the dataset page and to cite the related publication as well
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, ready-to-use citation string in repository-recommended form, with the DOI matching the record identifier, and an explicit statement of the dual citation expectation for the data and the associated publication.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate with ARK persistent identifiers, EVI Evidence Graph Ontology provenance serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, dataset schemas in JSON-Schema; conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; instances carry B2AI ontology terms
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted against named community standards with the serializations specified, and the enum value RO_CRATE gives the claim a machine-readable form alongside the prose.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: CM4AI project portal at https://cm4ai.org/ described as including documentation, data releases, tools and training; data releases page at https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; Cell Mapping Toolkit documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation links are specific rather than a single homepage, and cover the project portal, the release archive, the pipeline user documentation and a framework tutorial with installation instructions.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met, same external evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of (four prior releases), is_described_by (two preprints) and references (the Nature multimodal cell maps paper), each with a target_dataset DOI and a name
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed with a controlled vocabulary and each target carries a resolvable DOI. Two entries carry source_caveats, one flagging that the portal's May 2024 release entry is not stated by any source to be the DOI given, the other explaining that the Nature paper studies a different cell line and so is a reference rather than a description of this release.

strengths: Identifier integrity is exact. The DOI, the id slot, the citation and the persistentId embedded in the landing page URL all carry 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, and the prefix belongs to the University of Virginia Dataverse that the record names as host.

Source conflicts are resolved on the record rather than silently. Four disagreements between the project portal and the Dataverse listing are named in source_caveats with the preferred source and the reason, including a release date discrepancy and an AP-MS availability discrepancy.

Claims are declined where the evidence does not support them. The record refuses to carry forward the 464-protein imaging count from the prior release because the June 2026 archives have identical sizes but different checksums, and it refuses to equate the Data Governance Committee the release names with the Data Access Committee the preprint anticipates.

Funding is documented to award-number precision across three funders, with the RePORTER core project, the supplement number, the application number, the principal investigator, the project period and the fiscal year award amount all recorded.

The non-human-subjects determination is coherent across every slot that touches it: direct_collection, human_subject_research, is_deidentified, sensitive_elements and regulatory_restrictions all agree, and each states its basis rather than asserting a bare boolean.

Limitations and missing data are disclosed with unusual candor, including that computed cell maps are absent from this release, that the protein panels across modalities overlap incompletely, and that the MuSIC processing steps described do not apply to the distributed artifacts.
weaknesses: No variable-level metadata anywhere in the record. Neither variables nor is_tabular is populated, so composition can be understood at the archive and modality level but not at the field level, costing a point in both Element 3 and Element 5.

No change log relating this release to the October 2025 release it supersedes. The record notices that the image archives were regenerated but does not describe it as an erratum, so a user upgrading cannot tell what changed.
The anomalies slot is empty and no measurement-level quality issues are documented, such as batch effects across the three imaging conditions or guide representation in the perturb-seq screens.

Two internal date and version inconsistencies go unreconciled: a project end of 2026-08-31 from RePORTER against a stated November 2026 end, and a top-level version of 2.0 against prior releases listed at version 2.1.
Distribution format is stated only as the ZIP container, with no internal file formats named, so a reuser cannot plan ingestion before downloading multi-gigabyte archives.
Software tools are named with repository links but no versions are pinned, even though the record asserts that the version used to produce each dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata.
Conflicts of interest are not addressed in ethical_reviews, and the publisher slot is left empty by a documented decision even though the citation names the repository explicitly.
recommendations: Populate variables with field-level metadata for the tabular outputs in the SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq archives, and set is_tabular, so the two lost points in Elements 3 and 5 are recovered by the same addition.
Add an errata or change-description entry stating what differs from the October 2025 release, and record the image-archive regeneration there rather than only in source_caveats.
Populate anomalies with measurement-level quality observations per modality, or state explicitly that none were identified and by what check, so the empty slot is a finding rather than a silence.
Reconcile the two project end dates by attributing each to its source and naming the preferred one, in the same form the record already uses for the June 2026 release date.
Name the file formats inside each archive and populate encoding where text formats are involved, so the packaging and payload layers are both specified.

Pin software versions for the Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE and the Integrative Modeling Platform, and add preprocessing entries for the released archives themselves rather than only for the MuSIC pipeline whose outputs this release excludes.
Record University of Virginia Dataverse as publisher with a caveat that the attribution comes from the citation the landing page prints, and add a conflict-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews.
